title: Thailand vs Cambodia: Which Should You Visit?
description: A data-backed comparison of Thailand and Cambodia based on Reddit discussions, real costs, weather data, and traveler preferences.

faqs.question: Is Thailand or Cambodia better for first-time visitors to Southeast Asia?
faqs.answer: Thailand is generally the easier first trip. Its tourism infrastructure is more developed — English signage is everywhere, the BTS/MRT in Bangkok is world-class, and the range of accommodation from $5 hostels to $500 resorts is unmatched. Cambodia is more raw and adventurous, which some travelers lo

faqs.question: How far apart are Thailand and Cambodia?
faqs.answer: Bangkok to Siem Reap is about 400 km. A direct flight takes just 1 hour and costs $60–100 one way. You can also cross overland via the Aranyaprathet/Poipet border (6–8 hours by bus from Bangkok, ~$10–15). Bangkok to Phnom Penh is about 660 km — flights take 1 hour 15 minutes ($70–120).

faqs.question: Is it worth visiting both Thailand and Cambodia on the same trip?
faqs.answer: Absolutely, and many travelers do exactly this. A common combo is 7–10 days in Thailand (Bangkok + Chiang Mai or islands) plus 4–5 days in Cambodia (Siem Reap for Angkor Wat + Phnom Penh). The Bangkok–Siem Reap flight is cheap and short. faqs.question: Which is cheaper, Thailand or Cambodia?
faqs.answer: Cambodia is slightly cheaper for accommodation and beer ($0.50 draft beers are common), but Thailand often offers better value for money — meaning you get more quality per dollar. faqs.question: Is Cambodia safe for tourists?
faqs.answer: Yes, Cambodia is generally safe for tourists, especially in Siem Reap and Phnom Penh’s tourist areas. Petty theft (phone snatching from motorbikes) is the main risk in Phnom Penh. Siem Reap is very safe and tourist-friendly. Thailand is considered slightly safer overall with better-developed tourist

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Thailand and Cambodia?
faqs.answer: Both countries are best visited during the cool, dry season: November through February. Temperatures are comfortable (25–32°C), humidity is lower, and rain is rare. March–May is brutally hot in both countries (35–40°C). The rainy season runs June–October in Cambodia and May–October in Thailand.

faqs.question: Do I need a visa for Thailand and Cambodia?
faqs.answer: Thailand: Most Western nationalities get 60-day visa-exempt entry. No fee needed. Cambodia: You need a tourist visa — available on arrival at airports and land borders for $30 USD (bring a passport photo), or apply online for an e-visa. Valid for 30 days, extendable once.
